summary.title: Water Treatment SCADA
summary.description:
The system monitors water treatment. The web interface shows pH, water flow, chemical dosing, pump status and historical data. This model uses STRIDE to identify threats and suggest security controls.

The internal components and connections are assumed based on the screenshot. It does not confirm whether users can change settings. The dashed lines show trust boundaries, not confirmed firewalls. All threats are Open because the controls are proposed, not implemented.

data.name: Web user
data.description: External viewer, not automatically a trusted operator.

data.name: Web interface
data.description: Visible interface. RFB metadata suggests remote display; exact implementation is unknown.

threats.title: No login
threats.description: The screenshot shows "Authentication disabled". If this applies to remote access, someone could connect without logging in. The system would not know whether the person is an authorised user.
threats.mitigation: Require a username and password for each user. Only allow authorised users to access the interface and remove public access.

threats.title: Missing login logs
threats.description: If access is not logged and users do not have separate accounts, it can be difficult to know who accessed the interface. A user could deny having used it.
threats.mitigation: Give each user a separate account. Log successful and failed logins with the username and time. Only allow authorised administrators to change or delete the logs.

threats.title: Too many requests
threats.description: An attacker could send many requests to the web interface. This could make it slow or unavailable, preventing operators from seeing measurements and alarms.
threats.mitigation: Limit the number of requests and connections from each user. Restrict access to authorised users and keep a local interface available for operators.

threats.title: Wrong user permissions
threats.description: If the interface allows changes and user permissions are not checked, a user who should only view data could change pump settings. This could cause incorrect chemical dosing.
threats.mitigation: Separate users who can view data from users who can change settings. The SCADA server must check user permissions before accepting any change.

data.name: SCADA server
data.description: Logical monitoring and supervisory service; may share a host with the HMI.

threats.title: Missing change logs
threats.description: If setting changes are not logged, a user could change the dosing settings and deny doing it. It would be difficult to find out who made the change.
threats.mitigation: Log each setting change with the username, time, old value and new value. Protect the logs from being changed or deleted.

threats.title: Deleted logs
threats.description: An attacker with access to the server could delete logs to hide their actions. This would make it difficult to find out what happened and who was responsible.
threats.mitigation: Send copies of the logs to a separate server. Restrict access so users on the SCADA server cannot change or delete these copies.

threats.title: Getting admin access
threats.description: If the SCADA software runs with administrator permissions, an attacker who exploits a weakness in it could gain administrator access to the server. They could then change settings or stop the software.
threats.mitigation: Run the SCADA software with only the permissions it needs. Test and install security updates, and restrict administrator access.

data.name: Database
data.description: History is visible; a separate database/product is not confirmed.

threats.title: Changed stored data
threats.description: Someone with write access could change stored pH or dosing measurements. This could hide a problem and make the history shown to operators incorrect.
threats.mitigation: Only give write access to accounts that need it. Log changes to stored measurements and keep protected backups.

threats.title: Reading private data
threats.description: A user with more database access than needed could read stored measurements they are not allowed to see. This could reveal information about how the plant operates.
threats.mitigation: Limit read access to the data each account needs. Only allow approved accounts and the SCADA server to connect to the database.

threats.title: Storage full
threats.description: An attacker could cause many records to be saved until the database storage is full. This could stop new measurements from being stored and make history unavailable.
threats.mitigation: Limit how much data can be saved at once. Monitor free storage and send a warning before it is full. Remove old records according to a retention plan.

data.name: Controller
data.description: Local control logic, receives measurements and operates dosing equipment.

threats.title: Too much network traffic
threats.description: An attacker could send too much network traffic to the controller. This could prevent it from receiving settings or sending measurements to the SCADA server.
threats.mitigation: Use firewall rules to allow only necessary connections to the controller. Limit incoming traffic. Keep local pump control working if the connection to the SCADA server is lost.

threats.title: Changing controller program
threats.description: If programming access is not protected, an attacker with network access could gain permission to change the controller program. This could make the pump add the wrong amount of chemicals.
threats.mitigation: Require login and check permissions before allowing program changes. Only allow programming connections from approved computers.

threats.title: Fake controller
threats.description: If the server does not check where measurements come from, an attacker could pretend to be the controller and send false values. Operators could then believe the water treatment is working normally.
threats.mitigation: Check the controller's identity before accepting measurements. Use firewall rules to only allow the expected controller connection.

threats.title: Changed measurements
threats.description: An attacker could change measurements sent from the controller to the SCADA server. For example, a false pH value could hide a problem with the water treatment.
threats.mitigation: Protect the connection against changes to data, using authenticated encryption where supported. Check measurement timestamps and warn operators when data is old or outside expected limits.

data.name: Settings
data.description: Logical data flow; protocol and deployed protections are unverified.

threats.title: Changed pump settings
threats.description: If settings can be sent to the controller, an attacker could change them during transmission. This could make the pump add too much or too little chemical to the water.
threats.mitigation: Protect the connection against changes to data. Only accept settings from the authorised SCADA server. Set safe dosing limits in the controller.

data.name: pH / water flow
data.description: Logical data flow; protocol and deployed protections are unverified.

threats.title: Fake sensor
threats.description: An attacker could replace a sensor with a fake device that sends false pH or water flow values. The controller could use these values and cause incorrect chemical dosing.
threats.mitigation: Restrict physical access to sensors and their cables. Check that connected sensors are approved devices. Compare measurements with a separate sensor to detect false values.

data.name: Data
data.description: Logical data flow; protocol and deployed protections are unverified.

threats.title: Public process data
threats.description: The public interface shows pH, water flow and chemical dosing values. An unauthorised person could use this information to learn how the plant operates.
threats.mitigation: Remove public access to the interface. Require login and only let authorised users view process data.

threats.title: Reading network data
threats.description: If the connection is not encrypted, an attacker on the network could read the data sent to the user. This could reveal pH, water flow and dosing values.
threats.mitigation: Encrypt the connection using TLS or a VPN. Check the server's identity before connecting.
